transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As you know, our central chilled-water pump P-2 failed during the morning shift, and several areas are currently without normal cooling. We've got a scheduled batch in the reactor suite today, and the packaging area and utilities workshop also rely on chilled water. I'd like to get a temporary cooling plan in place, but per our standard practice, we need to run the pre-work review covering process, maintenance, and environmental health and safety findings before we set up any temporary connections. Can each of you share what you know so we can get that review completed and the controls documented?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share my process calculation for today's Reactor R batch. It requires exactly 400 kW of cooling and a supply temperature no higher than 8 degrees Celsius. I completed this calculation during the batch review but haven't entered it in the production control record yet. This is critical for sizing whatever temporary cooling solution we put together.

transcript.text: I confirmed with the rental provider this morning that a temporary chiller rated at exactly 250 kW can arrive today. Pump P-1 can provide 300 kW after Valve V-17 is isolated. I also confirmed from the facilities piping record that P-1 and the rental chiller are compatible for combined operation on the reactor suite circuit, with no additional facilities assessment required. The rental unit requires exactly 6 hours for installation, and this vendor confirmation is not yet attached to the maintenance work order.

EHS requires barriers maintaining exactly 1.2 meters of clearance and a fire watch during installation.
